Dr. Hoke is the perfect professor for Calc 1 (if you took it in high school). He tends to lecture about the concept without giving many examples, and the homework often includes difficult variations on the concept. He's really helpful in office hours though and also a super nice person.
tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK | ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

comment: Being honest, Hoke isn't the greatest calc teacher. I took calc 1 in high school, and I pretty much use all of my past knowledge to do the work in this class. That being said, he's a super nice guy. You can retake quizzes as many times as you want until you're satisfied with the grade and the tests are not bad at all.

Hoke is a nice professor and doesn't assign mandatory homework. The tests were fair because they covered class material so if you show up and listen you should get an A. There is a quiz every Friday which makes people actually show up for class but they are so easy and a grade boost.
tags: Clear grading criteria | GRADED BY FEW THINGS | Caring

comment: He explains the material well and makes the information make sense. There are weekly quizzes, so make sure you are on top of the material. Gives lots of opportunities for practice of the materials.
tags: Respected | Skip class? You won't pass. | Clear grading criteria

comment: Harry (or Chip) Hoke is a really nice teacher. If you meet with him outside of class he is very helpful. I had taken calc in high school, but did not do very well in his class because there are only 3 tests and the final which comprise your entire grade (there are 2 quizzes and homework but they barely count). Not a good test taker?-- beware
tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK | GRADED BY FEW THINGS | Tests are tough

comment: Professor Hoke is a great guy and he will help you if you go to his office hours. But get ready to do a lot of learning by yourself because you barely learn anything from his lectures. Without introducing a subject and providing any notes or definitions, he will just go straight into examples when starting a new chapter. Frustrating class.
tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK

comment: Harry (or Chip, that's the name he goes by) is a great professor, and will do everything in his power to help you pass the class. He is always available to meet with outside of class and is very flexible. He can get a bit confusing, and his explanations almost always leave me more puzzled than before I asked him, but overall he's a great prof.
Dr. Hoke is eager to help for students who ask. Just be sure to ace the tests because they are your only hope for an A; he hardly gives any credit to the homework.

I liked Dr. Hoke. Sure, the class wasn't interesting, but he's the guy to get Calc out of the way. Fairly clear, has office hours if you need. Posts old tests which are similar to the ones he gives. I didn't take calc and I found his class easy. Final replaces lowest grade, which is nice. Good grading system. He's a bit dull so take his class later
He is a good guy but is not very good at explaining concepts to students. I have heard that he is helpful outside of class, but I never went to him for extra help.

He's a nice guy, but he requires students to be really independent and teaches the class as if everyone had already taken it in high school. Everyone who already took Calculus in high school is doing significantly better than those of us who did not. The tests are also significantly harder than the homework and there is a lot of nightly work.

You get what you put in in this class. His tests are easier than the homework but the homework is a lot! Not that hard of an A if you have taken the class before. I would definitely recommend him, if you have.

He is very nice and is always smiling, however, I did not like the way he taught the class. Many times he depends on the students to work on their own and get it right, but that is very hard in Calc I. He is helpful if you ask, but his tests were hard. There is a lot of homework but there is not enough time in class to go over it. Tough teacher!
always wear a smile on his face. half-hour homework each time. easy class for Chinese.
He is a great guy. However, I am not sure if he is the professor to go for Calc 1. He is reasonable in terms of grades but I would only recommend him if you have taken Calc 1 in high school

Does a great job explaining stuff in class, homework is a lot, at least an hour and a half, but it is usually straight forward stuff , you have to go to class, because each hw is graded and if you miss on class, you cant hand in hw and that can ruin your grade, tests are challenging but not impossible

Easygoing teacher, very good refresher class for anyone who's taken Calculus in high school. If not, he's very helpful outside of class and answers any questions during class, even the stupid ones. Test aren't too bad, he drops the bottom five or so homework grades, and his grading scale is a bit easier than most.

He is extremely good at what he does and explains the material really well.  Calculus was my weakness, but after taking his class, it has become my strength.  He is very systematic, coherent and helpful.  Take him if you've had little or no prior experience and want to develop a strong basic pool of calculus concepts.

Hoke can get off track sometimes and go quick through the material, but he is helpful in his office hours in explaining homework.  He is also very straightforward in his tests also and are easier than the homeworks.  Overall, a fair grader and helpful outside of class.
Prof Hoke is helpful outside of class, but in class, I felt he went very quickly through the material. Tests were much harder than the weekly quizzes. Overall, not bad for fulfilling the FSSR gened.

Hoke is one of the worst professors i have ever had. If you have not taken calc before- DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. He does not explain anything well. It only makes sense to people who I have prior background in clac. Those people end up getting 100s on almost everything. The rest of the class is stuck wondering whats going on.
good teacher. very easy.

This class requires a lot of independent student. His homework assignments take a very long time and are worth a significant portion of your final grade. He offers flexible office hours, but sometimes it's not very helpful. You have to do a lot of practice problems to do well.

So helpful! Goes out of his way to explain the material and does it in a way that is clear and relatable. I am not a math person and was worried about taking a math course but he has made this course so enjoyable.

Such a wonderful teacher! He is beyond helpful and teaches with enthusiasm. So kind and always does everything he can to help his students. If you go to his class, and pay attention, you are sure to do well. He gives a quiz every Fri which may seem like a bad thing but they are only worth 10 points and by the time the tests comes you are prepared!
dr. hoke is the best teacher ever! I never understood calculus in high school, but he makes it all so clear! LOVE this class!

Dr. Hoke is awesome!he can explain the things very well. and it is easy to catch up with his class. always willing to help us!and his tests are not that hard if you pay attention to his homework and pastpapers

Hoke was a great teacher. He was always so helpful, and if he wasnt clear, he always made sure you understood it during office hours. His tests are fair and you could really tell that he cared. I'd recommend him.
My favorite teacher of the semester!  Definitely take Dr. Hoke, he is a quality teacher.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE NEVER HAD CALCULUS BEFORE!!! I saw way too many people failing because they had never taken calc. For those of you who have taken calc, Hoke is an easy professor and teaches his calc class for students who have had experience in the subject. He as three tests, Friday quizzes, and a final.

He is a great guy.  If you study and work at it, you can do well.  However, if you have zero experience in the class beforehand, I understand how this may be a hard class for you.  The class is kind of taught for kids who have already taken it which is why I found it easy and enjoyed him as a teacher.
Worst professor I've had. He rushes through his lectures and only half teaches. When you ask questions sometimes he doesn't completely answer them. Please do yourself a favor and don't take him.

This teacher makes your core experience horrible! If you have the choice choose someone else to be your core teacher. He approaches literature from a mathematical perspective, which means he has no idea how to interpret the books.
A nice guy, but if you haven't taken Calc before you seriously cannot get a good grade in this class. Do NOT take him if you haven't taken Calculus previously.
Nice guy, but if you haven't taken Calc before do not take his class
His poor future core students. He grades papers like a math teacher. Actually, approaches everything like a math teacher (sometimes useful, usually not). Also makes students do daily reading logs.

Take this class if you took calc in high school. He is good at reinforcing things already learned, but not necessarily at new topics. Homework is not graded, unlike in other calc classes, but it helps if you do it. a very nice guy.

Dr. Hoke is a great teacher.  If you read the book and ask questions is class, you'll do fine.  DO THE HOMEWORK....he frequently takes questions just like the homework for tests.  If you can do the homework, an A on any 4 of his tests are easily attainable.  Also, do the practice tests and all other sheets...they help alot...really a great guy, too
He is really easy if you actually bother doing homework. Most people dont, and get C's. You can get an easy A by reading.

He's a relatively easy A if you took some Calculus in high school. However, you may struggle if you've had little exposure to Calculus. He doesn't give too much homework.There are 3 tests, a final exam, and a few small quizzes.

Dr. Hoke is a great teacher who has a passion for teaching and for mathematics. He has a very sophisticated sense of humor...I find all of his jokes extremely funny. I have repeated many of them to my friends! (Who also enjoyed them)

Everybody above is bitter because they suck at math.  He's a great guy who enjoys his subject and is willing to give any amt. of time in order to make sure his students learn.  He is clear with what he does and does not deserve to be attacked like above.
I don' think he's that bad-you just have to learn to ask questions.  He doesn't have enough time to explain everything in class
He is not that bad. These other reviews are too harsh. Granted he is not "easy," but you have to be able to understand the concepts of calculus. If you do, you will do well in his class.

Worst teacher ever...I used to be good at math and now I feel like a retard because I cant understand anything he is trying to teach.  Its pointless to even go to class because you have to teach yourself everything and I thoroughly regret not saving my calc notes from highschool.

He's a horrible teacher, and his examples make no sense.  Everyone is confused by the end of class and he never explains how to do the homework problems he just goes through the numbers instead of the thought process.  He thinks he's hilarious, but no one else thinks so.

Horrible teacher.  Laughs at his own horrendous joke and really should just stop teaching.  He just can't teach and just confuses people.  I feel bad for those poor souls who have never taken calc before.  STAY AWAY

Was blessed to have had the opportunity to take professor Berryhill's Property and Environmental law classes.  He kept you thinking and was a great friend in and outside of the classroom.

A great person without question!
tags: Amazing lectures | Gives good feedback | Accessible outside class

comment: One of the best all-around people you will find. If you ask for help he will give as much as required. Don't let his sometimes pompous perosna get in the way - he truly wants you to learn, not regurgitate. I'd take him for anything he chooses to teach.

His sense of humour is distinct, and he carries his deep convictions into his approach.  He evaluates equally, and immersing into the material without analyzing effects of possible character differences is productive.  He cherishes the way in which he can impact his students.

Berryhill teaches at Regent for bar prep and was my private tutor for the bar. I passed the bar, first time, because of him. If *you* put in the work, he'll bend over backwards to help you succeed, but he doesn't just spoon feed his students. He's also the most approachable prof I've ever had bc he doesn't take himself so seriously.

People seem to either love him or hate him. The midterm was very fair, but the actual class discussions can be a bit challenging.  He wants you to think a certain way, which can be a struggle sometimes.  Not taking Berryhill at least once would be a mistake.

Professor Beryhill is an amazing teacher.  There is no doubt that he is a very difficult professor, but the upside is that you will receive the best education under him.  Best professor, hands down, and he really cares.  He is also very knowledgeable of pop culture and has an impeccable sense of style... unlike Devin who wears ugly shoes.

Berryhill is hard, there's no question, but you've gotta love him anyways. The man knows his contracts (and his baseball statistics) and you will as well by the end of the semester. It will take a lot of work, and you will feel stupid most of the time, but he's one of the best. Take him if you can!
He is incomprehensible, but he has some great one-liners.
Berryhill is the best!  If you missed him in Property, take him in Land Use.  There is no one in Virginia who has the knowledge and ability to instruct than W. Wade.

"Tough but fair"?! He's not a tough grader. But he's such a poor TEACHER that its tough to learn from him. Sure he's smart and will answer questions outside of class, but I'm not paying to listen to him talk about how smart he is. I want professors who TEACH. Not spoon feed, not walk around with their chest puffed out, TEACH. And he can't.

Berryhill is the classic law school professor.  Take every class from him you can.  No other professor will make sure you know the material like him.  Sure he isn't easy, learning the law isn't supposed to be easy.  But, his grades are fair and he's the most entertaining professor at UR.

Truly a great guy with a wealth of knowledge, the trouble is absorbing that knowledge.  Loves to play "hide the ball" (regardless of his insistence to the contrary) and his exams are among the most difficult I have ever taken.  That said, if you take his class YOU WILL know the subject well, BUT IT IS IN NO SENSE the easy way to learn it.

Professor Berryhill is tough but fair. You need to prepare very well to get the most from his class. He does not just handout answers he ensures that you learn the material. He is helpful and will answer your questions outside of class.

If you want to learn Property, this is the course.  If you want someone to teach you, take someone else.  Sure he's tough, but by the end of class you will know the material.  This guy is what law school is all about.

From the class of 91.  I was just thinking about Prof. Berryhill and googled him and found this page.  The thing is that most of what is said here is true, but Sitting here almost 20 years later I can say I wish I could sit in his class again and learn some more.  Yes, he is a classic "Paper Chase" professor.  It takes years to appreciate him.

His "lectures" were completely useless, 1.5 hour rant sessions of the "I'm brilliant/You're stupid" variety. The best thing to do is to be as inactive in class as possible, hit the hornbooks, study guides and caselaw, and study only for the exam. Aside from Bar Review, you won't hear one piece of useful information come from his mouth to your ears.

The comments here separate the wheat from the chaff.  People who come to law school and expect to be taught will do poorly.  People who come to learn do well.  Berryhill is a law professor in the Paper Chase mold, and excels at it.
He's a puppetmaster... in a good way.  He challenges his students to find the best in them.
The quintessential law school experience

This is the best damn law professor in the state.  idf you want to pass the bar or even learn the law, this is the man who can prepare you.  If  you want to sit on your ass and read the outline your best friend's cousin did at W&M, dont waste your time. Success follows hard work.  THANKS BERRYHILL -

For whatever reason, he has been permitted (by the powers that be) to belittle and ridicule his students for years. The explanation:  He has tenure.  Not a good enough reason, but reason enough NOT to attend this law school.  This is unacceptable behavior for a lawyer, let alone an educator.  In his own words: "Get a life, stuuupid!"

A "classic" law professor. Be prepared for class, don't expect him to give you the answers. I studied and kept up on the material and I did well. Don't be intimidated by his in class demeanor. Talk to him outside of class and you'll see he's a really nice guy.

Definately does not spell ANYTHING out for you. But keeps you slightly terrified and entertained. Expect to learn most of it on your own and to use him as motivation to study rather than a means to learn. In the end he makes you think, which is different from learning a subject. Instead youget a lot of mental exercise and interesting words o wisdom

By far the best class I had in law school. It's not socratic, so you get to know the "real" Berryhill. He was always helpful and insightful - and he definitely made you think. He was willing to help on the papers, and he treats his students very well, even after they are out of his class.

Wade is great.  He does play hide-the-ball, so he's not always clear, but he forces you to figure the material out.  He's entertaining and always willing to talk or answer questions.  He is an integral part of the law school experience.

HATED this class. Berryhill has followers for some unknown reason, but pay them no mind. Hes full of himself and mean as a snake. His sense of humor is, admittedly, terrific. But that doesn't excuse the rest of it. Just get through it and avoid him for the
VERY full of himself, and he shouldn't be, because he's a horrible teacher.
A for entertainment.  F for instruction.  You are better off taking someone else if you are actually interested in the subject.
Superb. I felt frustrated and confused at various points in the class, but his methods work.  By the end of the class I knew the material cold. Take him if you can.
Prof Berryhill's environmental seminars are outstanding.  If that is your interest, take as many of his seminars as you can.

Great instructor, but has a "different" personality. Focuses on truly understanding the material versus rote memorization. I got a kick out of him, others did not. In my opinion he was one of the best first year professors.

If you plan to sit for the Virginia Bar, take his bar review course.  All comments above regarding law school classroom observations notwithstanding, this professor runs THE bar prep course in the Commonwealth!

once you understand his goal is to teach you how to learn rather than to spoon feed you the material he makes a lot more sense. as a first year class property is very hard but what he has to offer can make the rest of law school easier

If i were rating on entertainment Berry would rate high. But Im not, his rating is based on teaching ability and he sucks. Maybe if he spent less time preening and trying to confuse and more time explaining the concepts people would have a clue what the hell is going on.
do not take Berryhill if you can help it!  Definitely one of the worst profs I have ever had.
come prepared

He is a bad professor.  He may have been there for a long time, but he's stunningly in love with himself to the detriment of his effectiveness as a professor.  Very unclear in class, more 'ranting' than teaching, and you will leave this course more confused and knowing less than you did before it.
Class is somewhat interesting, but was very put off by Mr. Berryhill's belief that he is a.) God's gift to teaching law b.) God's other gift to once praticing law.
No Comments
do not go to class unprepared

I had to read 3 books for this class (all of which I did not read) and do daily discussion posts on them. At first, he was an extremely tough grader and I was scared for my GPA (and life) however, he loosened up at the end. I got a great grade on my final research proposal (A+), however, this class was extremely boring. I hate space and astronauts!

comment: Dr. Essid's class was the best English class I have taken. Extremely thought-provoking, he offers great insight, and the content he chooses is very enjoyable. He's a VERY tough grader (-10 points for putting the wrong character name), but we only had 2 papers. You can also only miss one class before points are deducted from final grade. Overalleasy

comment: I can see how Dr. Essid would be a tough professor for his normal classes. However, since 383 is a requirement for a writing consultant job, he really cares about his students doing well. comment: Joe Essid is the worth teacher that has ever walked this planet. He is boring in class and actively seeks to ruin students lives. Never take his classes

comment: I took two classes with Dr. Essid this past semester and ENGL 383 was a significantly different experience. I felt that the expectations and guidelines for our commentary was very confusing, but once we all figured it out for ourselves, the class was pretty easy. The midterm felt somewhat pointless and the final was essentially the same assignment.

Dr. Essid is an excellent professor who genuinely cares about the success of his students. He has unusual beliefs, but he is tolerant and interested in the opinions of others and takes all viewpoints seriously. He engages with his students in order to make them not only better writers, but better students overall.

Best professor ever. Caring, funny, and extremely intelligent. Will challenge you to do your best work and think outside the box. Does not put up with laziness. If you work hard, however, he rewards you. I took his Writing Center training class - he does grade that a bit easier than his other classes, but he is fair and always available to help.

Dr. Essid is an awesome professor. He is very engaging and really helpful. You do a lot of writing and sometimes he grades tough, but you will never  get a grade and not know why you got it. The class was really helpful too. The final project is very lengthy and hard.

My favorite professor so far!  He balanced our reading assignments with movies.  Very interested in the wellbeing of each student.  Tough but fair grader, he can tell if you wrote a paper the night before!  He emphasized the value of experiential learning; my favorite assignment was the road trip paper.  My idea of a true liberal arts-style eacher!
He's a hard grader and you'll do a lot of writing. However, he is extremely helpful and clear.Be prepared to do a lengthy final project and don't expect to get an easy A.
I had him for teaching writing course. Very helpful and engaged. He's what all UR profs should be. He can connect with students. I had him 10 years ago.

I had the chance to communicate with him in Spanish. Really nice guy, who is not only academically engaged, but also keenly intersted in the welfare of int students. I was glad to hear that he is interested in visiting Bulgaria. Even funnier, he thought I was a grad student, what a great compliment. I really loved the Spanish talks.

A great professor.  He always makes sure that everyone knows the details of each assignment.  He is really interesting and very passionate about writing.  He is a very tough grader, but at least he tells you what you did wrong and he prefers to meet with you about each paper.
Great class.  He's a great instructor, I would recommend him for any class.  Very liberal politically and loves to blab about anything.
Dr. Essid is a fun professor and teaches interesting classes. His book selection for courses is good too.

she assigns too many reading and writing assignments and projects.  If you are ill, she does not care.  If you do not follow your assignments she will fail you.  Her class is overwhelming and I would not take any of her classes again.

comment: Shannon is a good teacher & helps you a lot. She is a real focused. She assigns tasks each week. Warning: if you do not follow your assignments you will fail. ALOT of reading & writing. She Does not have a sense of humor. But overall good. I would'nt take her class again. It's over whelming

Shannon is a good teacher & helps you a lot. She is a real focused. She assigns tasks each week. Warning: if you do not follow your assignments you will fail. ALOT of reading & writing. She Does not have a sense of humor. But overall good. I would'nt take her class again.
She's outstanding!

Great teacher! LOTS of reading to do but if you follow through & complete all assignments, you shouldn't get anything less than an "A". She provides incredible guidance on all work...just ask her for it; she encourages it. She is also very patient & personable, creating a casual atmosphere that allows everyone to be more vocal & effective in class.
if you participate you will get a good grade.  pay attention to your reflective journal she doesn't stress it enough in class.  she is very helpfull

On the second day of class, he dropped a Kingdom Hearts reference. That is like totally all you need to know. He is my favorite. I love this professor. He is so good. He likes teaching. Perfect guy to take this class with - he gave great feedback and always willing to meet. Very responsive to emails. Looking forward to another class with him.

comment: If you put in the effort this class is an easy A. There are two 5 page papers, one debate, a midterm, and an online final. There is a lot of information covered on the exams, but most questions are easy. You don't need to read the textbook/buy it. All you need to know is in the slides and primary source readings. Sparacino is great

comment: Lecture heavy with some participation. Grades tough on papers but debate, midterm, and final are times to make up for that. Funny guy who cares about his students. Definitely recommend american gov with him!

Dr. Sparacino is very smart and knows what he's talking about. Each class is a lecture the whole time. Two 5- page papers, one debate, a midterm, and an online final. Tests are manageable as long as you study the material. He gives great feedback on papers and is available to help students outside of class. Class gave me a lot of knowledge.

comment: Enjoyed this class a lot. Was lecture heavy and had a fair bit of reading but not daunting at all. He was super nice and helpful when needed. Makes jokes in class so the class isn't totally a drag even though its a lot of lecturing. Would take a class with him again. You can tell he knows his stuff

Professor Sparacino is passionate about what he teaches. He makes a lot of self-deprecating dad jokes. The class is very lecture-based. Each student has to participate in at least one debate. comment: Sparacino is great. Class structure is reliable: lecture with some back and forth debate and conversation. comment: Hes an absolute goat, if youre interested in taking PLSC courses I highly recommend him. Grade is compromised of a debate, two papers, a midterm, a final, and general participation. comment: Solid teacher, discussions are opinionated in class and although she is clearly left-wing allows room for students to dissent. Allows rewrites for papers and homework is graded on completion  & are tri-weekly couple sentence journal entries that you can reflect on your readings with.

comment: Professor Boxer is very fair with grading and allows rewrites which is great. She definitely has strong opinions about certain topics but tries to acknowledge opposing points. comment: Prof Boxer is very nice and caring, but the lectures are extremely dense and not enough discussions. I think just reading the articles would be similar to going to class, and the grading is sometimes unclear. While she does care about her students, her office hours are not too helpful so you might have to teach yourself some material.

comment: Having very limited prior experience with Philosophy, I found this course to be difficult. The material was interesting but I found the essays to be very challenging to write. comment: I do not agree with the other reviews of this professor; maybe she changed the format of the class upon reading reviews because discussion is fair and balanced. comment: Sitting through this class is like watching grass grow. Paper grading criteria is very ambiguous, and her lectures are repetitive and un-engaging. As far as the class goes, it is so obvious her ideals lean strongly liberal that it is almost impossible to take a different stance on the issues she brings up.

comment: Prof. Beanland is great at leading workshops but the helpfulness of her feedback depends on your style of writing. Does a very good job of explaining things if you are struggling. As everyone else says, he doesn't give A's but if you do your lab reports with proper notes and documentation he will grade fairly. He also sounds like Tim the Bear from The Cleveland Show.
Dr. Kanters is really nice and very helpful. Lab is difficult but he is forced not to give out A's. As long as you put in effort you will do fine. Sometimes he talks really fast so ask questions!

Thick accent. Hard grader BUT he is forced to not give A's. It's the way lab works here. Talk to him about it and you will understand. Grades are all equalized so it should not matter much. VERY willing to help- go see him!! Watch our for the group presentation-he criticizes like crazy. don't stress about lab-just put in effort.
Refuses to give above a B+ on lab reports for no reason. Hard, but will try to help you understand. He has a very thick accent and is extremely smart so he can be hard to understand at times

Worst lab I've ever had. He talks about subjects that may never be covered in lectures, and he grades very hard. Kanters is incredibly smart, but he's incapable of relating the material to anyone else. Good luck if you have to take him.
It's the worst

Teaches at an unbelievably slow pace. Takes about 25 minutes worth of information and drags it out for a three hour lecture. He turned what should have been an interesting class into a class that I hated going to. It would have been a great class if he had just covered more material in each lecture and moved had a quicker pace.
No Comments
Not good. Don't take

If you take this class, make sure that you can do all the readings. If you don't do the readings, there's no way you can do well on the pop quizzes. Also, her tests are confusing in the way that they're worded. In comparison to other Soc classes, this class has a lot of work!
She gives many pop quizzes but is not clear or straight to the point in what she teaches.
Worst core prof I've had yet. Poor explanations and pop quizzes. Avoid.

Great professor.  Interesting topic, does give pop quizes.  Not hard to do well in this class. Interesting fact: she took us on a prison tour.  You should be interested in the topic of deviance, however to enjoy the course

Class was usually interesting and discussion was relaxed. Tests were very straightforward. Tough grader on papers. It wasn't necessary to do all the readings but she does give pop quizzes. Willing to be flexible with due dates. Overall a great class.

Briddell is an excellent professor. She is fair and willing to change around due dates if it is reasonable. I found the tests to be easy and homework was only about one hour of reading for each class period. Her classes cover interesting topics. She is tough when it comes to papers though

She is a great professor. She is very clear and concise in her lectures. She manages to incorporate the readings into the lecture without spoon-feeding the information. She is the best professor I have had at this university.

She's what you'd expect from a sociology professor. Easy to get off topic, but then again the class isn't very linear. As a math-science guy, it was just tolerable. Important tip: she likes her papers clear and to the point. Do the readings. There are little pop quizzes here and there. Class participation is a thing. Test are kinda difficult.

Prof. Briddell expects her students to engage themselves and read/do the assigned work. She is not difficult to understand if you're actually listening and I enjoyed her class. I would take a class by her again. If you work hard, her class won't be too challenging OR too easy.
The type of teacher to give a quiz about the readings on a Monday 9am
I found Ms. Briddell to be one of the least accomplished and professional employees I have encountered at UR. It's a miracle she still gets a paycheck.
Laine is a pretty solid teacher. Sociology was a pretty easy class. Her lectures were super boring though. Easy tests and a pretty fair paper grader
Avoid if you value your sanity and GPA.
she is a great professor. Great discussions, debates and fun topics to talk about. she is pretty harsh with paper gradings, but her tests are fairly easy.

Extremely intelligent individual who is passionate about what he does. He helps you with language without making you feel inferior or stupid at any time. Doesn't just give textbook assignments- he makes it come alive through poetry, music, etc.
Very good interdisciplinary class on theater in Spanish America. Beware: lots of reading and you will have to act. The lectures are challenging. I would take this class again.

Very helpful outside of class, you can literally sit with him and discuss what your paper will say. Somewhat difficult to understand and DEFINITELY repetitive in the course's schedule, but really enthusiastic about justice and politics and Chile! He was also really helpful with my study abroad questions, going above and beyond his job requirements.
Prof. Izquierdo is tough yet available out of class for clarification. His lectures are challenging.
Nice guy, tough teacher, can be very unclear when it comes to essays and tests. Didn't learn all that much

Very nice young professor from Chile. Easy to understand and very helpful. The class had interesting readings/films and was a pretty easy grader. He uses the same method over and over which gets redundant.

Babb's course is tough. He is very knowledgeable about the subject and will take every opportunity to tell a personal story of his--on topic or not. The class focuses essentially on taking 2 sets of notes--one on his lectures, one on the book. Basically you're taking two separate classes, one on the book & one on his stories. Tests are subjective.

A mixed bag.  Entertaining and outspoken, he’s full of funny anecdotes & tall tales.  Unassuming he’s not, as he’s big-headed & blunt.  While you’ve got to like his confidence & panache, I’m not sure he’s really a great “teacher.”  The project is rough unless you have inspired people in your group.  I’d give Babb a “B, (the same grade he gave me).
Professor Babb has some interesting stories but I learned very little about marketing from his class. Test questions are wordy and unclear.
Most material is from the reading and not discussed in class.

Professor Babb is the best professor I have had in the business school. He applies everything he teaches to the real world. His tests are challenging, but you will learn SO much in his class. You should definitely take his course if you plan to major in Marketing.

Best professor ever. I don't even know what my grade in the class will be and I, honestly, could care less. I felt that I really got a lot out of it and Babb is clearly very knowledgeable. Interesting class.
I did well and liked the class as it is not boring but you have to do A LOT of work outside class to do well.  Tests are super hard but at the end he tends to hand out random A's and stuff.

Hard professor and there is not much structure to the class.  Interesting discussions but often on things that do not appear on the tests.  Tests are very hard and its important to stay up to date in the textbook reading. Trying to cram the night before a test will not work. Gives annoying project.

Great Professor.  I believe one of the best marketing Professors in the country.  His real-world experience and success make all the difference.  He is a venture capitalist currently on his fourth or fifth start-up.  His guidance will take you far, even if you are not interested in marketing.

Class is definitely not an easy A. But Babb is helpful if you go to him outside of class. Tests are a combination of both textbook and lecture. Lectures consist of Babb talking, no powerpoints or writing on the board, about a subject not in the text. So you must be able to take good notes. Textbook is not gone over in class, must read on own.
Arrogant and self-absorbed.  He knows the material, but he cant convey it to students.

Spends more time taking about himself than the material.  There's essentially no work in the course and class is pointless until the tests, which have little to do with what he's taught in class.  Make sure you actually read the book and match it to what he's said as he'll change up terminology on tests between notes and class.  Final projet sucks.

Yawn! We had to do these pointless scholarly articles for review and PLEASE READ the text book in conjunction w/ his notes! Do NOT rely on those notes alone because you will NOT do well! Tests are hard! Assigns this tedious marketing project toward the end of the semester when all other assignments are due! Brags, "I'm so successful!"

extremely entertaining in class. and does a wonderful job of matching you up with a group for your project. you will have a real sense of accomplishment and will really have learned something when you finish this class

Considered dropping class after first test which I did quite poorly on but after that point I knew exactly what I had to do and was able to do it.  Looking back I'm glad I didn't drop the course since it was a valuable experience and Babb is one of the most interesting and down to earth professors at Richmond.
He loves himself.  Really, really loves himself.
Great teacher with enthusiasm and experience in the subject.  Tests are really tough, but you learn a lot.  Recommended for marketing majors. Tales of his own experience make it really cool.
always talking about his life and his stories but never about how hard the exam will be. STUDY Like HELL or YOu will fail his class

A great teacher - I wish he taught more upper level marketing classes! He has great stories, I really enjoyed the class, and although his tests are hard, he still gives plenty of As (even if you didn't always earn it). Participation and a good attitude is key - such a nice guy.
Kind of a fun guy to listen to talk...he has great stories...but his tests suck and the project is a lot of work

Douglass is awesome. Comes to class in a powdered wig, brings a bat, has students act out gang cases, including one student playing the part of a door. He is far from easy, and the closed book final sucks, but I formed my schedule around having him for Evidence and Crim Pro after having him for Crim Law.
Awesome in every way. Cares about students, cares about them learning, great guy, presents material clearly.
Great prof! Very nice and cute too! Don't be fooled by how easy the exam appears to be though. He's a tough grader.

Very tough final exam, very tough grader. He knows his stuff, but sometimes can't express it well enough. Plus, he acts like he's a kindergarten teacher, which can be good or bad depending on your personality.
Not only is he the hottest professor at U of R law but he is also one of the best. Incredible teacher who really cares about his students. And don't forget, he is sooo easy on the eyes.

Super nice. Makes fun of students and himself. Class doesn't make sense until the end. Broken into three sections (see syllabus). Cold calls, but moves on if you know nothing. Watch a few videos. One essay assignment due. A few other short assignments. Final was three essays mainly on statute mapping and agency deference. Helpful in office hours.
Great professor.  Always helpful.  Pretty funny too.
No Comments

Continuance of 1st semester. Pretty boring. Long (5hr) take home, open note exam at end (start early- save your labs from the semester). Class only lasts 2/3 of semester. Very helpful and nice in office hours. Class was about once a week for 50 minutes. Understands the class is boring for us, but tries to make it interesting and lets you out early.

Legal Research sucks in general. Class is 50 minutes once a week. Good thing they taper off as the semester continues. Full year class. Corriell is super helpful, clear, and passionate about her topic. She knows the class doesn't really care and tries to make jokes. This class could be worse; she makes it manageable.
Absolute legend.  Went too maybe 30% of the classes and got an A-.  I am probably one the most unartistic kids at the University.

this guy is crazy. started out assigning way too many assignments and then cancelled half of them because there wasnt enough time. couldnt handle a class full of 13 students and the mess that came with it. says you should spend a lot of time outside of class working, but to get a B doing the minimum is all thats necessary.
He is insane but still a pretty easy class

this class was ridiculous. i probably went to half the classes and am probably going to get an A...and im the most unartistic kid i know. if your works are decent and completed in a reasonable amount of time its impossible to get below a B. he is a really nice guy and if you get a bad grade you can talk to him and he'll most likely bump you up.

Definitely take his sculpture class if you are an unartistic student trying to get your art requirement done! As long as you try and your works are decent he'll give a B. Usually get out of class real early, don't have to come...such a chill class and chill prof

As a freshman in a class with mostly upper level art students, I felt comfortable yet challenged.  Mark helped with directing and guiding but still allowing me to make my own decisions with my peices.  A great instructor, especially if you need guidance on how to do art.  Great to fill a requirement because he grades based on his own directions!

Great Prof., even though he is teaching something outside of his expertise.  He really gets into the core books and helps his students to as well.  Class disucssions are great and he has taken us outside on really nice days, great atmosphere...really chill, awesome prof.
Class consisted of straight power points. Every single day. It was tough to stay engaged. The tests were tough and the averages were usually low. Would not take this class again.

material is interesting, however there are random pop quizzes that most people do poorly on and rubrics are posted after written assignments, lab is really fun - mostly outside, tests are based on class material and  pretty easy

I'm really interested in ecology but the class is very boring. Only uses powerpoint slides that are completely based on the text, but expects you to read the textbook and come to class. She does a poor job answering questions and making the content meaningful. The first exam average was a 74. She has a lot to learn as a first year teacher.
She is really a sweet lady. Have had private lesson with her for 2 years and enjoy the class with her.
No Comments

Easy teacher. No attendance policy. Just be prepared and she will absolutely love you. Accent barrier can be difficult with her. And as for the piano technique she teaches (I wanted to learn jazz technique)... it sucks (she uses the Russian method. very uncomfortable)
Dr. Meyers helped me with chemistry during my freshman year, and sparked my love of science for the rest of my college career. He will always be remembered as a part of the UR family

comment: Dr. Myers is the epitome of a fantastic college professor. It's actually mind-blowing how good this guy is. Dr. Myers is easily one of the smartest men I've met, he is super friendly, and his lectures couldn't be better. Very communicative, can be easily reached through email, always helpful, and well-prepared for class every time without fail.
He is going to be one of the most memorable professors. He brought Chemistry to my life again. He lighted up my passion again....Great man! I respect him as my grandpa.
Dr. Myers is really helpful and clear!
Dr. Myers is amazing! Take him for chem 141!
He is the best!

Professor Myers was a really good teacher and taught in a way that helped you to learn the subjects rather than memorize at all. Very easy teacher if you simply do 3 or 4 old tests the night before the test and understand the questions in them.

Professor Myers was hands down my favorite professor of my first semester at UR. He is really nice, helpful, and funny! As long as you work hard you will do fine. Study those online tests and see him during office hours

Absolutely great teacher, and an even better guy. His course is difficult, however. Much harder than the other Chem 141 classes. You must be willing to put in a lot of work, especially if you never took AP chem. I was getting murdered early, and worked very hard to salvage a good grade. I learned more in this class than any of my others, however.

Dr. Myers is  a WONDERFUL teacher! He really tries hard to make class interesting and I am coming away from his class with a much better and thorough comprehension of chemistry. His tests and assignments are definitely doable and he always offers help session multiple times a week for anyone needing them. Take his class if possible!
Dr. Myers is awesome! He made me fall in love with this subject again! :) He is a little strict but as long as you study hard, you will be ok. And his old tests online really helped a lot!
Dr. Myers is tough, but extremely helpful. If you put forth the effort in his class you will do well. Really great guy and funny too.

Dr. Myers is an amazing and genuine man with a heart of gold. His class isn't easy, but its chemistry so don't expect it to be. He is more than happy to help you if you're struggling. He holds help sessions weekly (go to them). His teaching style isn't for everyone, but his stories are amusing. WIth effort, you should have no trouble passing

Loved Myers! Yes, the class is difficult, but if you pay attention in class, take notes, actually put effort into the problem sets, and utilize the old practice tests....you are guaranteed to do well! Class was always interesting and I gained a greater appreciation for chem after taking this class!

Myers is great! He challenges his students which may be frustrating at first but it allows you to understand the material at a much deeper level. He also has so many stories that make learning the material much more enjoyable and his study sessions are extremely helpful. I would definitely take his class again!

If you use the old tests that he has on his website you will do well in his class. Take adequate notes during lecture and attend his study sessions if you're confused. He's a fairly lenient grader and will give you points for attempting problems! I really enjoyed his class.

Myers expects you to study and work hard to receive a passing grade. Make sure to use the book and his website with old tests to study and you'll do great. I recommend taking him if you actually want to be brilliant!

Myers expects you to study and work hard to receive a passing grade. Make sure to use his site with old tests to study and you'll do great. I recommend taking him if you actually want to learn the stuff!

Nice guy with very interesting stories pertaining to chemistry.  Difficult teacher though who does not explain many concepts as in-depth as you need for the tests.  Review sessions helped me learn the concepts better.

Myers is a tough teacher, but he really does try to help you through your confusion. He's stories are always entertaining, but you sometimes miss the reason for them. All in all he's a great person and really tries to help you understand the material. If you pick him as a teacher,make sure you get a tutor to even out the rough edges
He saved me in chem. He took the time to teach the material. He only really gives out B and B+ but it is worth it

This class was very unhelpful. He gives problemsets about every other class and a lot of the times he doesn't explain the technique to solving the problemsets even though it's a grade. He tells stories, but they generally don't make sense and the class could go much quicker and easier without them. Save yourself the grief and take the other teacher
Oops below i messed up on my helpfulness rating!
His test are definitely difficult but he puts in the time to help you learn and understand.  Go to ALL of the review sessions, class, and study all of the notes and old test and you will do well.

Is he difficult? Sure. But his lectures are totally entertaining- he's got humorous insights into alot of concepts that other teachers I've had just glaze over. It's refreshing to be in a science class where I'm not falling asleep or choking on my own saliva from boredome.
He is a great teacher. Lectures are interesting and he expects you to be at all of them and pay attention. Very hard grader, but worth it for the MCATs
absolutely awful.  his "help" was confusing.  i wish goldman was there to save me.
loved how he made us all feel stupid for not knowing coulombs law...yeah that was definitely our fault
ummm CONFUSING!  what kind of person would think this guy was any good? sorry i don't have everything from 141 seared in my brain

He is HARD. In the end, however, it is worth taking his class as he forces you to learn the information. I complained about the difficulty of his classes until I took the MCAT. I got almost all the questions right on the material that he covered. He forces you to learn information in much more depth than is normally required.

Best lecturer in the Chem Department. He's very energetic and you leave every class feeling the same energy for the subject. He's hard, so pre-med kids with little interest in chem might not like him, but he's great for anyone else with interest in the subject.
he is a very good teacher. as long as you don't procrastinate and keep up with class notes; you'll do fine. if you fail his class, it's really you...
dr myers is great! very helpful. i don't think he's as hard as people say he is. study, and you'll do fine. the final was a little rough, but the class was well worth it. highly recommended!
Random and sometimes funny stories that seem to have nothing to so with chem, that he somehow makes work.  Not easy, but still highly reccommended!
myers is totally incomprehensible and makes you feel stupid.  i can't believe i paid money for this class.  he's useless.

Yeah he might be entertaining...but when you get the test you realize that all his dumb bs stories didn't quite explain something like d-orbital splitting with the depth he demands...you just sit in class and piles of information flow over you.

Myers knows his stuff, however he will present it in the most convoluded way possible.  Exams will have large amounts of Chem 141 minutae on them, b/c he expects you to have remembered EVERYTHING from two years ago.  If you go for help, you will get the same unhelpful musings and bizarre examples.  Take Goldman for your sanity.
This man gets so excited about chemistry that you have to get excited about it as well. He's a hard grader but he'll teach you lots. Highly recommended.
Dr. Myers is an awesome professor.  He is hard, but you definately learn in his class!
he will do his share and if you do yours, you will be fine and do well.  a very good teacher.
A really hard teacher, who moves very very quickly, but also definitely very helpful, especially if you go after hours to see him. Overall, worth the work!
No Comments
Definitely one of the hardest professors I encountered at Richmond, but an amazing teacher who definitely knows what he's talking about
One of the best profs I ever had in my undergrad or grad chemistry career.  THE reason I became a chemist.
No Comments

A really hard teacher.  Knows more about chemistry than anyone I've ever met, but sometimes it seems like its difficult for him to relate this down to beginning chemistry students. Completing his class prepares very well for next level chemistry classes
She's the worst professor I had ever met. She does not understand what her students needed and teaches whatever that bored you.

Terrible terrible terrible. A professor who can't explain anything,spending most of her time talking about irrelevant things that has nothing to do with the thesis she's been teaching. Everyone gets a B+ first, than she started to give a uniformly A- at your second paper.

Professor Harbin is extremely disorganized and flighty. I found her class very boring, especially since it was pure lecture even though she said it would be discussion-based. She is also fairly pompous toward students.

You can barely recognize her handwriting. You won't be able to take notes from her writing. She can do nothing but to confuse you, no structural organization of class material. Dropped the class at the first week. Don't take her class or you will regret.

Class discussions can be boring at some times, but other times they evolve into interesting debates. You really have to pay attention to make sure you understand the material. Only coursework was 2 papers and short responses to readings plus an exam. She is very willing to help out with papers and to make sure you understand. Easy for an FSLT.
fair
Excellent professor. Loves the students, loves teaching. Walks you through everything.
Gives you practice tests, not hard at all.

comment: I took Multivariate Calculus, and it was my favorite class so far in college. It is not an easy subject, but if you try, Nall will give you the best grade possible for your work. A lot of the reviews are negative, but I feel that reflects more on the difficulty of the the course.   Nall is life.

Awesome guy, but he's the type to not understand why you couldn't possibly understand an abstract mathematical topic instantly.  Lectures were also very scattered and confusing, although interesting.  Basically taught myself out of the book the entire semester (which is an excellent one, by the way).

Dr. Nall is an extremely helpful and funny guy. And a great mathematician (he is an expert in topology). However, his lectures are hard to understand and he jumps here and there. But at least his tests are easy. It's easy to get a 100, but also easy to get an 80. Small mistakes on the test will lose you massive points. Extremely handsome guy though
Dr. Nall has a very loose, relaxed way of having class and discussion that end up making it like a Math seminar course - which is pretty dope.

I essentially taught myself the entire course. He was super helpful, but couldn't explain anything. I had already learned most of the material from taking physics courses, but he somehow managed to make me confused. His tests are very straightforward, no tricks at all, but know that you WILL have to read the book.

I taught myself the entire semester. His tests and weekly quizzes feel like they have nothing to do with what you're learning until the end of the year. You have to find someone to help you understand the concepts or you will fall behind.

Nall is not a very good professor.  He is a nice guy, but he speeds through lesson plans.  He explains the what of the course, but does not spend time on the why.  If you are good at calc already you will enjoy the class.  If you have not taken it you will probably struggle and I would look elsewhere.

He is a very nice person and willing to help, but the subject is challenging and he teaches fast. office hours are important. He is not a tough grader. do well on the weekly quizzes because they really help. Attendance is not mandatory but its necessary if you have never taken the course
easily best (and chillest) math prof ive had @ UR...material is tough but he presents it clearly

he is too busy playing with this tools in class and does not do a good job explaining the lesson! his notes are already pre-written in his computer that he just plays in class. this is not very helpful in teaching students who are learning calc3 for the first time.
This guy is great at explaining the lessons. You will learn it the first time if you pay attention.
goes over problems people had in the homework, if you understand all the homework and old tests and quizzes it is not too bad, although it is calculus

Van is a really nice guy but a little unclear though with his teachings and expectations.  He is very understanding with this though and will walk you through troublesome pts.  I would recommend him for Linear Algebra, i got an A.
he moves too quickly and mumbles when he explains problems

TERRIBLE at teaching- his examples were poor. tests were not too hard, but as someone who took calc in high school and did pretty good back then, i was disappointed with my semester grade. do your homework!

Dr. Nall posts old tests online so you know what to expect on tests, he wants everyone to get an A, and as long as you study you should be fine.  He is funny and will always help you outside of class- if you took calc in high school you'll get an A.

i'm in the middle of taking his class right now.  It started out shaky, but he's progressively doing better.  He is very helpul and his little quirks make class interesting.  Class goes by pretty fast.. the routine is always the same.  My only complaint is the lack of detail in which he goes through homework and lack of examples when teaching.

I've only had this man for 2 days, and I can already tell I'm in for a horrible grade because of him.  Nothing he teaches helps me on the homework and not even the book helps me with the homework.  He doesn't spend any time explaning anything and just keeps moving on, regardless of how lost everyone is.  I was good at calc before him...

unwilling to help, very unclear.  I think the problem is that he is so smart and he doesn't know how to transfer his knowledge to others.  Looks down upon his students and is very degrading if you don't understand.  His courses were difficult, but he didn't make them any easier because he was so hard to follow.  His tests came out of left field and most of class time was spent watching him try to do examples on the board.  He made what could have been interesting classes very boring and mundane.

Dr. Nall was a great prof for "Explloring Human Relations." Out of all my years at UR, I remember the most from this class with him. Even more than what I learned in my major field of Political Science.

Well, he's a cool guy, but he's kind of unclear about a lot of concepts and sometimes it's not even worth listening because he only contradicts himself.  Overall, he's a decent teacher and cares about his students for the most part.

Terrible teacher.  Lost half a semester's homework.  Didn't even write his own tests.  See previous comment about his "examples" that are incorrect homework problems and borrowed problem sets from other teachers.  Probably brilliant but shouldn't be in front of students.

He teaches by examples, but doesn't prepare any of these examples ahead of time.  Half of the class is often spent watching him try to figure out how to do his own problem that he just made up on the spot and then correcting a bunch of mistakes that he makes.  You have to teach yourself everything.
If you like hating math, or if you are a sadomasochist take him. Otherwise, choose another prof
He's basically a rocket scientist, really smart, kinda over your head sometimes.
nice man, terrible teacher. uniquely boring with little to no personality. take him if you do hw and like to teach yourself

Really nice, and gives alot of points for going to office hours. However he is really unclear and hard to follow in class.
SO confusing, take him if you like teaching yourself
H.S. calc made no sense to me, but taking it with Nall was great. He is super nice and was very helpful outside of class. His final was also super-easy.

very dry, except on rare occassions when he has so much chalk all over his hands/shirt/pants that everyone starts laughing....the class is very difficult too...you have to take a lot of time out of class working on problems

Prof Nicholson is the one to take for your language requirement! He cares about your success and is extremely clear and helpful! Easy to get an A if you put your time and effort into it! Best decision taking this class 1st semester fresh year! HUGE GPA boost and great transition into college! My favorite professor yet :)

Best professor i've had at richmond so far (1st semester freshman). I absolutely love Prof. Nicholson. He cares about his students and makes sure everyone thoroughly understands the topics covered. He is clear, helpful, and makes class fly by. Taking LAIS 221 with him was the best decision i've made here! Hope to take more classes with him!!!!
Chillest professor ever. Great quality and teaching techniques combined with super chillness. Def take him you wont regret it
This class was great and he's a great professor, whether you need to take 221 for the gen ed or plan on moving on in spanish this is a great class to take!!

Very nice, easygoing guy. My class got quite attached to him. He makes you participate, but not in a hard or intimidating way(ie. speak to others, read aloud) Do your homework and study and you'll do well. Quizzes are fine, and only on vocab, tests he gives you helpful study guides. Not a boring class, as he has you up and speaking often.

This instructor may know computing, but he lacks the necessary skills and ability to teach. He was never adequately prepared for class-he winged it. He was unable to explain information such as the subject content, assignments, etc. in an organized, clear and concise manner. His deameanor was nervous, high strung and impatient.
didn't have him for a class, but he's always been very helpful with computer stuff on campus.  If I wasn't so dumb, I'd take his classes, but he would skool me too bad

She does not allow any extra credit. The only reasons that you get low grades is because she is super critical and not clear or specific when explaining an assignment. Then when you submit what you think that she wants she then gets all specific of what she wanted. Also, side-note, she speaks German and expect you to understand.

Pretty easy. Writes outline on the chalkboard in beginning of class. Straightforward. Graded midterm. Optional (not really) paper at the end. Final exam is essays and MC (MC are worth 2/3 of grade). Likes 'loss of consortium' and product liability. Talks about football. Not the clearest, but torts is pretty easy to figure out. Look at past exams.

Professor Swisher is a great, intelligent professor. He is really funny and his method of teaching is is very straightforward. He does socratic cold calling, but the class is mostly lecture.  We had a graded midterm, a final and an optional 6 page paper. His exams are hard, but not unfair.
Took every class he taught, great man, not a fan of lewd and lacivious co-habitation
